name: Chiffon Grace (シフォン グレイス)

claims.text: Wheat-free claim is worded for the シフォン生地 (batter) specifically; no dedicated/certified whole-kitchen statement was found, so cross-contact is unconfirmed.
Not applicable — dessert/bakery shop.
Uses 地養卵 eggs throughout; not vegan.
Owner explicitly aims for cake 'everyone can eat safely,' driven by her own health experience.
Rice flour throughout, including handmade rice-flour cookies in the orange sandwich; no wheat flour or white sugar in the batter.

name: Miron Rice-Flour Bakery (ふぁすとふーど＆お米パン miron)

claims.text: パンはすべてグルテンフリー — no wheat flour is used on premises; listed in Japan's national all-GF bakery guide as a wheat-free bakery (★★★★).
Rice-flour and specially-cultivated Koshihikari rice are the base for bread, bento, onigiri, chiffon and cookies.

Bento items (e.g. stewed hamburger, karaage) may involve seasonings/coatings — as an allergy-focused rice-flour shop these are intended to be wheat-free, but confirm the specific bento before ordering if highly sensitive.
Most breads are egg-free and several are dairy-free vegan; a few items are free of all 28 major/minor allergens.
Shop was founded specifically to serve a child's egg/milk allergy, and its concept is food that allergy families can eat with confidence.
Wheat-free rice-flour bakery listed in the national GF bakery directory; egg-free and partly vegan; run by an allergy-parent owner.
Entirely wheat-free facility with in-house brown-rice milling; no wheat flour is handled on site, so cross-contact is minimal.
Bakery items; savory rolls use soy but products are labelled 小麦・卵・乳不使用 (no wheat). Confirm any tamari/soy component if highly sensitive.
Products are wheat-, egg- and dairy-free and vegan-friendly; whole bakery is plant-based.
Founded by an allergy parent specifically for allergy families; cookies made free of all 27 designated allergens.
「小麦、乳、卵不使用のパン生地」 and cookies 「特定原材料27品目不使用」 - dedicated GF, allergen-conscious bakery listed in empacede's fully-GF guide.
No wheat, eggs, dairy, or nuts are used anywhere in the workshop, making it a fully wheat-free production environment.
Many items are egg- and dairy-free by design and dedicated vegan (soy-milk) cakes are offered, but some products such as pizzas use additive-free cheese, so confirm the specific item.

The shop was founded specifically to serve people with food allergies and deliberately avoids the seven mandatory allergen ingredients, so staff are highly allergy-aware, though no individual-order cross-contamination protocol was documented in reviews.
100% domestic Koshihikari rice flour, additive-free, leavened with house-made apple yeast; no wheat gluten used.
Entire workshop is free of wheat, egg, dairy, and nuts, which is rare and reassuring for celiac and allergy travelers.

The entire shop is gluten-free / wheat-flour-free, so it is one of the safer choices in Kyoto for celiac and gluten-intolerant diners. The one documented exception: the Miyako Monaka has cross-contact on its production lines, which the shop states on the menu, so celiacs should avoid that specific item. Everything else is made without wheat flour.
Described by gluten-free travel guides as a completely gluten-free bakery and pancake cafe, including gluten-free versions of Japan's famous souffle pancakes.
All sweets in the shop are made without wheat flour.

Vegan options are limited. While the menu is built on plant-based red bean paste, many signature items contain dairy, including the An de cheesecake (cream cheese) and pancakes/treats served with butter or cream. Vegan diners should confirm which specific items are dairy-free before ordering.

Because the shop is entirely wheat-flour-free, the menu itself flags the one cross-contact item (Miyako Monaka), which suggests allergen awareness in how items are labeled. No further detail on staff training was found in available reviews, so confirm directly for severe allergies.
A rare 100% gluten-free / wheat-flour-free shop and cafe, well regarded by celiac travelers; staff are repeatedly described as gentle, polite and helpful.
Signature gluten-free souffle pancakes are made to order and consistently praised; a safe way to enjoy a treat that is normally off-limits to gluten-free diners.

name: Ikkakuju Karasuma (100% GF izakaya — okonomiyaki, karaage, yakitori)

claims.text: The restaurant presents itself as 100% gluten-free across its entire food menu, which greatly reduces the risk of wheat in the kitchen; however, no source documents specific cross-contamination or shared-surface protocols, so confirm griddle/teppan handling with staff if you are highly sensitive.
One diner reported it is '100% gluten free except for some of the drinks,' so check beverages separately.
The restaurant states that all dishes are gluten-free including the seasonings, which implies a wheat-free (gluten-free) soy sauce is used rather than standard wheat-based soy sauce.

Not vegan-friendly: the okonomiyaki is Osaka style and contains fish meat even in plain orders, and most items are topped with bonito flakes. As one reviewer warned, 'they contain fish meat (even if you order a plain flavour) as they are Osaka style. They also top most items with bonito flakes.'
The okonomiyaki batter itself is made with dashi (fish/bonito broth), so the base is not vegan.
The complimentary starter is fried tofu topped with bonito flakes, another reason vegans should confirm options directly with staff.
The restaurant was founded specifically so that children and people with wheat allergies could eat safely, and developed its rice-flour recipes with that goal, indicating allergy-aware cooking.
Staff are described by visitors as friendly and professional, though one review noted occasional miscommunication, so be clear when ordering.
Entirely gluten-free food menu using specially cultivated 'Nikomaru' rice flour in place of wheat, with okonomiyaki, takoyaki, rice-flour noodles, karaage and teppanyaki all gluten-free.
Celiac and gluten-free diners report eating safely here; one called it a 'fantastic little place' that is 100% gluten free apart from some drinks.
The restaurant states all dishes are gluten-free down to the seasonings, so condiments like soy sauce are accounted for.

This is a fully dedicated gluten-free establishment: the kitchen handles no wheat products at all, and wheat-containing items are not allowed onto the premises, which strongly limits in-house cross-contamination.

The owner cautions that, because trace wheat contamination during the manufacturing of Japanese ingredients cannot be completely ruled out, those with severe wheat allergy should refrain (重度の方はお控えくださいませ). Highly sensitive celiac diners should weigh this and confirm directly.
The kitchen uses gluten-free soy sauce rather than standard wheat-based soy sauce, and seasons with fermented staples like salt koji and rice miso.
Multiple sources confirm gluten-free soy sauce is used throughout the menu.

Vegan options exist but are limited; the place is gluten-free first, and most of the menu contains animal products. Reviewers report vegan versions of curry and white stew, plus salad, soup, grilled vegetables, and soy milk ice cream.

One reviewer described roughly four or five vegan dishes available, suggesting vegans should ask which items are prepared vegan; no specific reports on vegan cross-contact were found, so confirm with staff.
The owner is personally wheat-allergic and the head chef follows a gluten-free diet herself, so allergy awareness is central to how the place operates.
The owner openly advises that severe wheat-allergy cases should refrain, showing transparency about the limits of what a no-wheat-on-premises kitchen can guarantee.
Entirely gluten-free cafe and bar: wheat flour is replaced with rice flour, gluten-free soy sauce is used, and even the bar-time dishes and drinks are gluten-free.
No wheat is handled in the kitchen or permitted on the premises, making it one of the safer gluten-free options in Kyoto and frequently recommended for celiac diners.
Diners praise the gluten-free fried chicken, curry, desserts, and gluten-free cocktails, plus friendly staff and a relaxed atmosphere.

The entire establishment is 100% gluten-free: the kitchen states it uses no wheat, barley, oats or rye anywhere on the menu. Because no gluten-containing ingredients are present in the building, the usual sources of cross-contamination are largely removed — though the venue is not explicitly described as a certified celiac-dedicated facility, so those with severe celiac disease may wish to confirm prep details directly.
Every dish is gluten-free and vegan, including the two pasta dishes, which are made with 100% corn penne rather than wheat pasta.
CHOICE uses tamari shoyu (gluten-free soy sauce) in its cooking instead of standard wheat-based soy sauce, and the soup broth is made without fish flakes.

The kitchen is entirely plant-based — no meat, fish, eggs, dairy or honey are used anywhere on the menu — so vegan cross-contact risk is inherently minimal since no animal products are present in the kitchen at all.
A reviewer noted that staff were very helpful with allergy information and that English is spoken, making it easier to confirm dietary needs.
Widely recommended as one of the best places in Kyoto for vegans, vegetarians and gluten-free eaters, where the whole menu is safe to order from.
A diner summed it up simply: 'Everything is gluten-free!' — the entire menu is both gluten-free and vegan.
